binders: Universally quantify over a finite index type ι; it may be empty.
Universally quantify over a measurable space Ω and a probability measure μ on Ω.
Universally quantify over a family of real-valued functions X : ι → Ω → Real.
Universally quantify over real parameters lam and t.
hypotheses: For every i in ι, X i is Borel-measurable.
The indexed family X is mutually independent under μ.
The parameter lam is strictly positive.
For every i in ι, the function ω ↦ exp(lam · X i ω) is μ-integrable.
conclusions: The real-valued probability of the event {ω | ∑_{i∈ι} X i ω ≥ t} is at most exp(-lam · t) times ∏_{i∈ι} ∫ exp(lam · X i ω) dμ.
mathematical_definitions: S(ω) = ∑_{i∈ι} X i ω is the finite pointwise sum of the family.
M_i(lam) = ∫ exp(lam · X i ω) dμ is the real Bochner integral, equivalently the exponential moment under the stated integrability hypothesis.
The tail event is the inclusive one-sided event {S ≥ t}.
The right-hand side is exp(-lam · t) · ∏_{i∈ι} M_i(lam).
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every finite mutually independent family of measurable real random variables on a probability space, every positive real exponential parameter lam, and every real threshold t, if each exponential exp(lam X_i) is integrable, then the probability that the sum of the variables is at least t is bounded above by exp(-lam t) times the product of their exponential moments.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The index type is finite but is not required to be nonempty.
For an empty index type, the sum is 0 and the product is 1; the conclusion becomes P{0 ≥ t} ≤ exp(-lam · t), while measurability, independence, and integrability assumptions are vacuous.
The parameter lam must be strictly positive; lam = 0 and negative values are excluded.
The threshold t is arbitrary and is not required to be nonnegative.
For negative t the upper bound may exceed 1 and therefore may be non-sharp, but the proposition still asserts it.

No centering, identical-distribution, boundedness, moment, or direct integrability assumption on X i is imposed beyond measurability, mutual independence, and integrability of exp(lam · X i) at the selected lam.
The exponential-integrability hypothesis is specific to the chosen value of lam; the proposition does not assert it for other exponential parameters.
Mutual independence of the whole indexed family is assumed, not merely pairwise independence.
The bound is stated for the supplied lam and does not take an infimum or optimize over lam.
The event uses a non-strict threshold and is one-sided; there is no absolute value around the sum.
Because μ is a probability measure, Measure.real of the measurable finite-sum event has the intended finite real probability interpretation.
The explicit integrability hypotheses prevent the nonintegrable default behavior of the Bochner integral from affecting the right-hand side.
ambiguities: The supplied one-level body of ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun refers to kernel independence without expanding that internal predicate; it is interpreted here as mutual independence of the indexed functions.
The supplied body of MeasureTheory.integral is opaque beyond its type and owner module, so its interpretation as the Bochner integral relies on that supplied declaration information.
The target does not separately state measurability of the finite-sum tail event, although the individual measurability hypotheses support it.
No claim is made that the displayed bound is optimal in lam or informative for every threshold.
